_note: First-pass flavour for the imported catalogue, merged into data/pool.json by tools/merge-flavor.mjs. Prose only — never mechanics, which the card renders from the entry's own channels. Hand-edit freely; the merge only fills entries whose `text` is still null unless --force is passed.
annihilating-resonance: The note finds the pitch a body breaks at and holds it there.
battered: Something gives all at once and the ground arrives sooner than expected.
bisected: The cut does not stop where cuts stop.
bleeding-cut: A thin line opens and takes its time deciding how much to bleed.
bloody-mess: More blood than the wound has any right to produce, and all of it visible.
brittle-flesh: The cold goes all the way in. Skin has the give of old porcelain now.
broken-arm: The arm bends where no joint is, and stays bent.
broken-back: Something deep in the spine lets go with a sound felt more than heard.
broken-finger: One finger points somewhere the others do not.
broken-foot: The small bones go together, in a bunch, like dry sticks.
broken-hand: The hand closes wrong and will not open again.
broken-jaw: The jaw hangs slack and every word turns to noise on the way out.
broken-leg: The leg folds mid-stride and takes the rest of the body with it.
broken-neck: The head sits at an angle the neck was never meant to allow.
broken-rib: A rib goes with a wet click and every breath afterwards finds it.
broken-skull: The skull gives under the blow and does not come back.
broken-toes: The toes crumple in the boot, and the boot keeps them there.
broken-wing: A spar snaps midway out and the wing folds against itself.
bruised-tail: The tail takes the blow full and hangs heavy afterwards.
bruised-wing: The membrane blooms dark from the impact and will not catch air.
bruising-blow: The limb takes the weight of it and goes dull and useless.
burned-feverish: The burn goes past pain into something like fever, and the shaking starts.
burning-radiance: Light kindles under the skin and burns outward, patient and clean.
carbonized: What is left holds its shape until something touches it.
catch-fire: The flame finds cloth, then hair, and settles in.
caved-cranium: The blow lands square and the shape of the head changes.
chopped-neck: The blade goes deep into the neck and stops against bone.
cleaved-ankle: The ankle opens and the foot turns loose beneath it.
cleaved-appendage: The limb parts most of the way through and hangs by what is left.
cleaved-finger: The blade takes the finger at the knuckle, cleanly.
cleaved-forehead: The steel splits the brow and lodges in the bone above the eyes.
cleaved-hand: The hand comes apart along the line of the cut.
cleaved-muscle: The cut goes through the muscle wall and the strength drains out of it.
cleaved-neck: The blade finds the neck and takes nearly all of it.
cleaved-tail: The tail opens along its length and hangs by a strip of hide.
cleaved-wing: The wing splits from edge to shoulder and folds in on itself.
clipped-foot: The blade catches the foot on the way past and takes something with it.
collapsed-chest: The chest gives inward and does not fully rise again.
compound-fracture-back: Bone comes through the skin of the back, white and wrong.
compound-fracture-finger: The bone comes out through the knuckle.
compound-fracture-foot: Bone pushes out through the top of the foot.
compound-fracture-hand: The bone breaks and keeps going, out through the back of the hand.
compound-fracture-rib: The rib snaps outward and opens the skin from the inside.
consuming-brilliance: The light gets in everywhere and leaves nothing to hide behind.
consuming-void: Something reaches in and takes years rather than blood.
corrosive-wound: The acid finds a seam and keeps working long after the splash.
critical-internal-bleeding: Nothing shows on the outside. Everything is happening under it.
crushed-appendage: The limb flattens under the impact and never quite comes back.
crushed-larynx: The throat collapses and the next breath has to be fought for.
crushed-leg: The leg is pulped from hip to knee and the shape of it is gone.
crushed-shoulder: The shoulder caves in and the arm hangs from ruined moorings.
crushed-torso: The blow drives the chest inward and something inside gives with it.
crushed-wing: The wing flattens under the blow, spars and all.
crushing-blast: The air itself hits like a wall and something in the chest yields.
crushing-blow: The limb takes the full weight and the shape of it changes.
cut-brachial: The point finds the artery inside the arm and opens it.
cut-deltoids: The shoulder muscle parts and the arm drops, dead weight.
dazing-blow: The world tilts and takes a moment finding level again.
dead-leg: The leg goes numb from hip to knee and stops answering.
declawed: The blade takes the toes off at the root, all together.
deep-corrosion: The acid works past skin into the meat beneath, quietly.
deep-slice: The blade goes in deeper than the wound looks from outside.
destroyed-organs: The blow lands and something vital stops working behind the ribs.
destructive-resonance: The sound settles into the bones and keeps shaking them.
disemboweled: The belly opens and does not keep what it was holding.
dislocated-knee: The knee goes sideways and every step negotiates with it.
disoriented: The world keeps turning after the head has stopped.
encased: The ice closes over and there is no more air behind it.
eviscerated: The torso opens from side to side and the ground catches what falls.
flash-frozen: The cold arrives all at once. Nothing moves after it.
fractured-tail: The tail breaks mid-length and trails uselessly behind.
frostbite: The cold takes the feeling out of the extremities first.
frostburn: The cold burns going in and keeps burning after.
funny-bone: The whole arm goes to static from elbow to fingertip.
grazed-lung: The point nicks the lung and each breath comes back a little short.
grazed-scalp: The scalp opens and blood finds the eyes almost at once.
gut-punch: The blow lands under the ribs and takes the air with it.
hamstring: The blade goes behind the knee and the leg stops holding weight.
head-cracker: The skull gives with a sound nobody in earshot will forget.
holy-unmaking: The light does not burn. It simply decides the body is finished.
horrific-scar: The wound will close. It will not close neatly.
impaled-gut: The point goes into the belly and stays there.
impaled-stomach: The blade drives through the stomach and lodges against the spine.
jarring-blow: The impact runs up the limb and leaves it ringing and useless.
jaw-dropped: The blade takes the jaw and the face is suddenly the wrong shape.
jolted: The muscles all fire at once and none of them agree.
kebabed: The weapon goes all the way through and stops on the far side.
kebabed-appendage: The limb is run through end to end and the weapon stays in it.
knocked-down: The legs go out and the ground comes up.
laid-to-the-bone: The cuts go down past the meat until they find something white.
liberated-skeleton: The acid takes everything that was not bone, and takes it quickly.
life-drained: Something reaches past the body and takes from what is behind it.
lightning-rod: The charge finds a path straight through and takes it.
lodged-weapon: The blade goes into the arm and will not come back out.
lodging-blow: The weapon buries itself in the limb and stays.
mortal-blow: The blow lands exactly where a body cannot afford one.
muscle-lock: Every muscle seizes at once and none of them will let go.
neural-overload: Thoughts arrive out of order and none of them finish.
nicked-achilles: The point catches the tendon behind the heel and the leg buckles.
nicked-carotid: The point grazes the great vessel of the neck. Grazing is enough.
nicked-femoral: The point finds the artery high in the thigh and opens a seam in it.
nicked-tendon: The point catches a tendon in the wrist and the grip goes slack.
numbed-tail: The tail goes dead from the base and drags.
obliterated: The force arrives from every direction at once.
overhead-slash: The blade comes straight down and the skull takes the whole of it.
persistent-acid: It clings. Water spreads it, and it keeps eating regardless.
pierced-calf: The point goes through the calf and out the other side.
pierced-heel: The point goes through the heel and the tendon goes with it.
pierced-hip: The point drives into the hip joint and stays lodged in bone.
pierced-knee: The point goes into the knee and the joint stops being a joint.
pierced-lung: The lung is opened and every breath whistles where it should not.
pierced-muscle: The point goes through the meat of the arm cleanly.
pierced-organs: The point finds something soft behind the ribs and opens it.
pierced-skull: The point goes through the skull and into what it was protecting.
pierced-stomach: The stomach is opened and its contents go where they should not.
pierced-throat: The point opens the windpipe and air goes out the wrong way.
pierced-wing-base: The point drives through the wing where it meets the body.
piercing-blow: The point goes in clean and comes out red.
pinned-arm: The blade goes through the arm and holds it where it is.
pinned-leg: The point drives through the leg and fixes it in place.
pinned-tail: The tail is nailed down and every pull makes it worse.
plucked-eye: The point takes the eye out of its socket entire.
pulped-appendage: There is nothing left in the limb holding a shape.
pulped-leg: The leg is meat and bone fragments in a sleeve of skin.
pulped-shoulder: The shoulder is no longer a joint. It is a bag of pieces.
pulverized-leg: The bones of the leg come apart into gravel.
pulverized-shoulder: The shoulder shatters into pieces too small to name.
pulverized-spinal-column: The spine comes apart under the blow, vertebra by vertebra.
pulverized-tail: The tail is crushed flat along its length and hangs dead.
pulverized-wing: The wing is broken in a dozen places and drags like a net.
punctured-aorta: The point opens the great vessel above the heart.
punctured-brow: The point goes in above the eye and blood curtains down over it.
punctured-carotid: The neck opens and does not stop opening.
punctured-cheekbone: The point lodges in the bone of the face and sticks fast.
punctured-face: The point goes through the face and the world goes white for a moment.
punctured-heart: The point finds the heart, and the heart stops arguing.
punctured-hip: The point drives deep into the hip and the leg gives up.
punctured-lung: The lung collapses around the wound and breathing becomes work.
punctured-muscles: The point goes through the arm in more than one place.
punctured-neck: The point opens the neck and the breath goes with the blood.
punctured-tail: The point goes through the tail and out the far side.
punctured-wing: The point opens a hole clean through the wing.
punctured-wrist: The point goes through the wrist and whatever was held is dropped.
puncturing-blow: The point sinks in deep and pulls back out slowly.
radiant-annihilation: The light burns away everything it can reach and looks for more.
ribboned-torso: The chest is opened in a dozen places, none of them shallow.
ringing-ears: A high tone arrives and crowds out everything else.
rung-bell: The head takes the blow and the lights go out for a while.
ruptured-eardrums: Something bursts deep in the ear and the world goes muffled and sideways.
ruptured-organs: Something behind the ribs tears and keeps tearing.
sapped: The strength goes out of the limbs and does not come back.
scalped: The blade takes hair and the skin under it in one pass.
seared-flesh: The skin blackens and splits, and the pain arrives a moment late.
searing-light: The light burns the eyes before they can close.
set-alight: The fire has found something it likes and settled into it.
severed-appendage: The limb comes away and the ground catches it.
severed-arm: The arm is gone at the shoulder and the shock arrives before the pain.
severed-biceps: The muscle of the upper arm parts and the arm hangs slack.
severed-ear: The ear comes away and the side of the head goes hot and wet.
severed-femoral: The great vessel of the thigh is opened and empties fast.
severed-fingers: Fingers come away and land somewhere out of sight.
severed-foot: The foot comes off at the ankle and the leg finds nothing beneath it.
severed-hand: The hand comes away at the wrist, still holding what it held.
severed-leg: The leg is taken above the knee and the world turns over.
severed-muscles: The muscles of the arm are cut through and the arm stops answering.
severed-nose: The blade takes the nose flush with the face.
severed-quads: The front of the thigh opens and the leg will not straighten again.
severed-tail: The tail comes away and lies twitching where it fell.
severed-tendons: The tendons of the leg part and the foot goes loose.
severed-wing: The wing comes away at the joint and the sky is gone with it.
shattered: The force arrives and the body has no answer to it.
shattered-arm: The bones of the arm break in several places at once.
shattered-back: The spine breaks and everything below it goes quiet.
shattered-eye-socket: The bone around the eye caves in and the eye goes with it.
shattered-foot: The foot breaks into pieces inside the boot.
shattered-hand: The hand breaks in more places than it has bones to spare.
shattered-leg: The leg breaks in several places and folds in the middle.
shattered-neck: The neck breaks and the head is only along for the ride.
shattered-rib: The rib breaks into pieces and the pieces go inward.
shattered-skull: The skull comes apart along seams it did not have before.
shattered-vertebrae: The bones of the tail break through and the tail goes dead.
shattered-wing: The wing bone breaks in multiple locations.
shredded-pectoral: The chest muscle is opened in overlapping cuts.
signature-slash: The blade takes its time and leaves something worth reading.
skewered-arm: The arm is run through end to end and pinned to nothing.
skewered-tail: The tail is run through lengthwise and stays that way.
skewered-wing: The wing is punched through at the joint and will not fold.
skewering-blow: The point goes all the way through the limb and out the far side.
slashed-arm: The arm opens along its length and the grip fails.
slashed-brow: The brow splits and the blood goes straight into the eyes.
slashed-eye: The blade crosses the eye and the eye does not survive it.
slashed-eyes: The cut crosses both eyes in one pass and the world goes dark.
slashed-pectoral: The chest opens and the arm loses its anchor.
slashed-tail: The tail opens along its length and bleeds freely.
slashing-blow: The edge opens a long wound that immediately begins to run.
slashing-sweep: The blade takes the legs and the ground follows.
sliced-calf: The calf opens and the leg will not push off it.
sliced-muscle: The muscle of the arm parts along the cut.
sliced-tendons: The tendons part and the fingers stop obeying.
sliced-wing: The wing opens along the membrane and spills air.
slit-wrist: The wrist opens and empties faster than it should.
soul-rend: Something leaves that was never meant to, and something else moves in.
sprained-wrist: The wrist turns past its limit and whatever it was holding is gone.
staggering-blow: The blow lands and the legs need a moment to be convinced.
stunning-blow: The head snaps back and nothing arrives behind the eyes for a while.
system-shock: Everything the body runs on stops at once and has to be restarted.
tendon-slash: The blade goes behind the leg and the leg gives out.
tissue-liquefaction: The acid stops eating skin and starts on what skin was covering.
vorpal-cut: The edge goes through as though the body were not there.
waning-vitality: Something is taken that has no wound to show for it.
winded: The air leaves all at once and takes its time coming back.
